summary: Verified the WhatsApp status-callback round-trip fix end-to-end. Backend: 5/5 pytest tests pass — (1) POST /api/webhooks/twilio-status with the known pre-existing SID SM01776c2435e0c04f064082872fe90b53 + MessageStatus=failed + ErrorCode=63005 returns 200 and updates the whatsapp_messages row; GET /api/whatsapp/messages?phone=+15166057352 (admin) now returns that message with status='failed' and error_code='63005'; (2) freshly-sent outbound via POST /api/whatsapp/send → simulated Twilio callback → list endpoint reflects status='failed'/error_code='63005' on the same id; (3) POST /api/whatsapp/send does NOT 500 (returns 200 with message object including twilio_sid); (4) /api/whatsapp/conversations returns 200 list; (5) status webhook is safe for unknown SIDs (still returns 200). Frontend: logged in as owner admin (tracyfortune@islandhoptt.com), opened /admin → WhatsApp tab (admin-whatsapp-content visible), opened conversation for +15166057352. wa-thread shows 14 messages; 9 outbound messages render wa-status-<id> (mix of 'queued' for older sends pre-fix and 'failed' for the 3 messages whose status callbacks have arrived); the 3 failed outbound messages each render wa-error-<id> with the exact red note: 'Not delivered — the customer is outside WhatsApp's 24-hour window. Business-initiated messages require an approved template.' Inbound message ('Hi IslandHop') still displays correctly. Regression: conversations list still loads (55 entries) and whatsapp-no-convos only shown on empty.
action_items: Optional UX: pre-existing 'queued' outbound messages (the 6 oldest in the +15166057352 thread) will remain stuck on 'queued' label forever because they were sent before the status_callback wiring landed and Twilio will not retroactively call back for them. Consider a one-time admin reconciliation script that hits Twilio's REST GET /Messages/{sid} for any whatsapp_messages where status='queued' AND created_at < <fix deploy time> to backfill final status. Not blocking — new outbound messages will populate status correctly via the now-active callback.
Optional: surface the 'queued' state with a softer color (currently text-muted-foreground) so admins know it's pending and not stuck; already implemented this way.
critical_code_review_comments: twilio_client._status_callback_url() correctly prefers TWILIO_STATUS_CALLBACK_URL and falls back to FRONTEND_URL + /api/webhooks/twilio-status. Verified that the webhook endpoint exists at /api/webhooks/twilio-status (server.py ~L8115) and processes both MessageSid+SmsSid / MessageStatus+SmsStatus shapes.
Status callback handler stores both an update on whatsapp_messages and an audit row in twilio_status_events — good observability. Returns 200 with empty body to keep Twilio happy.
Webhook is idempotent against unknown SIDs (no-op update + log) — verified test_webhook_unknown_sid_is_safe passes.

AdminPanel.js wa-error-<id> note correctly handles BOTH error codes 63005 (no open 24h session) and 63016 (template required) — both are the typical Twilio codes for this scenario; sensible defensive coding.

Minor: list_whatsapp_messages returns msgs with no count metadata; if a thread grows beyond 100 (default limit) older messages would silently disappear. Consider returning {messages, total} or supporting pagination. Not a blocker for this fix.

context_for_next_testing_agent: WhatsApp status-visibility loop is fully working end-to-end. Test artifact: /app/backend/tests/test_whatsapp_status_iter21.py is a self-contained regression suite — re-run with `pytest backend/tests/test_whatsapp_status_iter21.py -v`. Frontend selectors confirmed: [data-testid='admin-tab-whatsapp'] (tab), [data-testid='admin-whatsapp-content'] (panel), [data-testid='wa-thread'] (message list), [data-testid^='wa-msg-'] / [data-testid^='wa-status-'] / [data-testid^='wa-error-'] (per-message). rca of the issue: Original RCA (confirmed by tests): the admin dashboard showed outbound WhatsApp messages as permanently 'queued' because /api/whatsapp/send saved msg_doc.status from twilio_client.send_whatsapp()'s initial response ('queued') but the Twilio REST messages.create() call did NOT include a status_callback parameter. Twilio therefore had no URL to POST async delivery updates to, so the row never moved past 'queued'. When Twilio later failed the message with error 63005 (recipient outside 24h WhatsApp customer-care window — free-form business-initiated messages require an approved template), the failure was invisible to the dashboard. FIX (implemented and verified): (a) backend/twilio_client.py now resolves _status_callback_url() (TWILIO_STATUS_CALLBACK_URL > FRONTEND_URL/api/webhooks/twilio-status) and passes it as status_callback on every real Twilio create() in _real_send_sms + _real_send_whatsapp; (b) POST /api/webhooks/twilio-status updates whatsapp_messages.status + .error_code by twilio_sid and writes a twilio_status_events audit row; (c) AdminPanel.js wa-thread now renders status next to each outbound message AND a red wa-error-<id> note explaining the 24h-window/approved-template issue when error_code is 63005/63016. Mitigation verified end-to-end via test_whatsapp_status_iter21.py and live Playwright run.
